newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: De Beers held talks with Zairean rebel boss Kabila.
newsitem.headline: De Beers held talks with Zairean rebel boss Kabila.

text.p: The firm which controls the world's diamond market, South African diamond-mining giant De Beers, held weekend talks with Zairean rebel leader Laurent Kabila, the company said on Monday.
De Beers has trading offices in Zaire's diamond capital Mbuji-Mayi, which is in the hands of Kabila's Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire (AFDL).
It also has an office in Kisangani, which is also controlled by AFDL rebels fighting to overthrow President Mobutu Sese Seko.

"De Beers can confirm that its representatives met...Mr Kabila over the weekend to discuss its concerns relating to the protection of its staff and facilities in the areas now controlled by the alliance," De Beers said in a statement.
It gave no details on the content or venue of the talks.

Most of the eastern half of the mineral-rich Central African country is under the control of Kabila's fighters, and analysts said the De Beers talks were a further sign that Mobutu's government had become irrelevant.

De Beers has a contract to buy the production of the MIBA (La Miniere de Bakwanga) mine at Mbuji-Mayi, which is 80 percent owned by Mobutu's government, with Belgium's Sibeka owning the remaining 20 percent. De Beers holds 20 percent of Sibeka.

Kabila's rebels now have Zaire's second city, Lubumbashi, within their sights. The copperbelt city was braced on Monday for the arrival of Kabila's fighters after news that they had taken the town of Kipushi, less than 30 km (20 miles) away.
